READABILITY.evidence: The format doc comment and helper comments are clear. Business logic uses many single-letter locals, though: `n := d.readUvarint()`, `l := &Loop{}`, `p := &Polygon{}`, `g` and `cs`. That is idiomatic Go, but the cap limits this to accept.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: shapeindex_encode.go is 619 lines, over the 500-line cap. It ignores the convention: per-shape encode/decode sits in this file, not next to each type in lax_*.go and loop.go. It adds a parallel `shapeKind` enum instead of using the existing typeTag mechanism. The functions themselves are short.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Every count is checked against a limit (readCount, maxEncodedCells), and slices are preallocated only up to `min(n, decodeChunk)`. Shape and cell IDs must be in range and in order, bools are strict, and edge IDs are range-checked. Decode leaves the index unmodified on error, truncation maps to errShapeIndexTruncated, and the index is locked.

C7-11-CASE1.evidence: The change only adds ShapeIndex.Encode/Decode. Existing typeTag values and per-shape wire formats are untouched; it uses a private shapeKind instead of adding tags. The Shape interface is unchanged. The only edit to existing code is the internal pendingAdditionsPos fix in applyUpdatesInternal.
